topic: Systematic Cleaning Procedure for a Vacant Departure Room
questionText:

Hence, option (C) is correct.

questionText:
Read the following consumer protection and regulatory enforcement case study and answer the questions that follow:

A commercial health supplement brand, 'MaxiHeight Pro', launches an aggressive multi-media advertising campaign on national television and social media. The advertisements feature a celebrity sports star claiming that consuming their powder guarantees a height increase of 6 inches in adults aged 20 to 35 within 90 days. A coalition of consumer activists and pediatrician associations lodges a formal complaint before the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA). The CCPA's Investigation Wing, headed by a Director-General, conducts an inquiry and establishes that the claim is biologically impossible, scientifically bogus, and constitutes a 'Misleading Advertisement' under Section 2(28) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The CCPA exercises its statutory powers: ordering immediate discontinuation of the advertisements, imposing a financial penalty of Rs. 10 lakhs on the manufacturer, directing full refund to all purchasers, and prohibiting the celebrity endorser from endorsing any product for a period of one year.

options.text: Under CPA 2019, celebrity endorsers are held accountable for misleading claims unless they can prove due diligence was conducted to verify efficacy.

detailedSolution:

Under CPA 2019, celebrity endorsers are held accountable for misleading claims unless they can prove due diligence was conducted to verify efficacy.

questionText:
Read the following consumer protection and regulatory enforcement case study and answer the questions that follow:

A commercial health supplement brand, 'MaxiHeight Pro', launches an aggressive multi-media advertising campaign on national television and social media. The advertisements feature a celebrity sports star claiming that consuming their powder guarantees a height increase of 6 inches in adults aged 20 to 35 within 90 days. A coalition of consumer activists and pediatrician associations lodges a formal complaint before the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA). The CCPA's Investigation Wing, headed by a Director-General, conducts an inquiry and establishes that the claim is biologically impossible, scientifically bogus, and constitutes a 'Misleading Advertisement' under Section 2(28) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The CCPA exercises its statutory powers: ordering immediate discontinuation of the advertisements, imposing a financial penalty of Rs. 10 lakhs on the manufacturer, directing full refund to all purchasers, and prohibiting the celebrity endorser from endorsing any product for a period of one year.

Question: Under Section 2(28) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, what legally constitutes a 'Misleading Advertisement'?

options.text: An advertisement that falsely describes a product, gives false guarantees, or deliberately conceals vital material information to deceive consumers.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Definition of Misleading Advertisement.

options.text: An advertisement that omits the statutory registration details and complete manufacturer address on outer retail packaging.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: An advertisement that compares product pricing and technical specifications directly against a rival brand in the market.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: An advertisement that utilizes promotional discounts and limited-time introductory offers to attract prospective purchasers.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Resource Management (Definition of Misleading Advertisement):
An advertisement that falsely describes a product, gives false guarantees, or deliberately conceals vital material information to deceive consumers.

Detailed Context:
Under Section 2(28) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a misleading advertisement is defined as one that falsely describes a product or service, gives false guarantees, or deliberately conceals vital material information, thereby deceiving consumers. Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
